why: Rule 1: the 40.6 cm mu shows a monotone template-following Bragg rise to 130k at 3001, so it cools toward 3002, where a 2.1 cm 133k proton stub also attaches; the 151 deg prong pair drops it one tier.
Heuristic 8: all four candidates are isolated single sub-cm dots spread 200-300 cm apart with no fitted segment and no readable direction anywhere in the event, so any click is as good as any other.

Two independent monotone Bragg ends on different particle types (p rises x2.52 to 171k at 10000 over its whole 22 cm, mu rises x1.81 to 128k in the last 5 cm at 10001) with the cool minimum at the 10002 junction they both point away from.

The 8001/65012 pair is a 175 deg break in one continuous 255 cm track, not a junction, and 8000 is a clean monotone Bragg stop, leaving 65011 as the only non-stopping free end and the lowest-z point; but its 105k tip peaks 1.5 cm in, so it could equally be a cosmic entering near the cathode.

Rule 1 at a 72 deg junction: the 11.6 cm heavy prong spikes to 360k at its far end 8000 (stopping proton) while the 19.4 cm MIP prong leaves the other way, and both prongs carry a charge blob in their first bin at 8002.

The only real track (32.8 cm, 100-130k proton-like) declines monotonically away from its Bragg stop at 11000, so 11001 is its start, and a blip cloud from the surrounding shower sits there including 92048 at 3.7 cm.

Rule 1: the 228 cm muon has a monotone 175k Bragg rise over the last 25 cm at 10000, so it cools all the way back to 10024, which sits mid-volume at the lowest z with a 7 cm off-axis blip 40018 and nothing continuing past it.

3001 is the mid-volume end of a flat-MIP 145 cm track that exits at the z=500 downstream face, and a cloud of 1-3 cm blips (30012, 28008, 32016, 75020) sits within 7-8 cm of it; the 200k proton stub 70 cm away is unattached to anything.

Deg-3 junction in an otherwise shower-only event: a 3.5 cm 94k stub one way, a 15 cm e-shower plus a 6.5 cm mu the other, and a 4.5 cm 105k prong tipped at 270k (stopping proton) 9 cm along the stub direction; the 164 deg pair keeps it off certain.
Textbook three-prong vertex with 56/71/97 deg openings, all prongs forward in z: a 20.1 cm proton rising x1.53 to 181k at 12005, a 10.7 cm proton, and a 24.7 cm MIP muon, all radiating from 12004.

Cross-cluster pooling: 77016 and 17001 are 9.4 cm apart, so cluster 77 and 17 are one ~400 cm muon that stops at 17004 (x2.29 rise, with the 12 cm and 4.8 cm sub-MIP Michel segments beyond it), and it leaves 77017 at 101 deg from a 24 cm proton that Braggs to 163k at 77015.

Rule 1 with two independent Braggs: the 381 cm muon is flat MIP for 350 cm and rises monotonically to 235k at 12000, while the 7.4 cm prong rises to 158k at 12001, so both cool toward 12002, which sits at the lowest z with the muon running forward in z.
Degree-4 junction with well-spread 24-116 deg openings, including an 18.8 cm proton that rises x5.86 from 34k at the vertex to 197k at 10001; nothing else in the event competes.

The far end carries a smooth 8-point Bragg tail (141k down to 80k over 4.3 cm at 9000) plus a 0.9 cm Michel-like blip 5.7 cm beyond, so by rule 3 that end is the stopping end and 9001 is the start; but a lone 276 cm track starting 15 cm below the top wall and going down at 46 deg reads just as well as a stopping cosmic.

Rule 1 on the only fitted object: the 42 cm track shows a clean monotone template-following Bragg rise (50k to 245k over the last 3.5 cm) at 9001, so it is the stopping end and the track cools all the way toward 9000; low confidence because that leaves a single prong with no second prong anywhere and the remaining candidates are structureless sub-cm blips.
